# Pātimokkhaṭṭhapanakkhandhaka (Kd 19)
**ID:** Kd 19
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Pātimokkhaṭṭhapanakkhandhaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-kd19
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m3.mul8.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Pātimokkhaṭṭhapanakkhandhaka* ("The chapter on the cancellation of the Monastic Code") is the nineteenth chapter of the Khandhaka division in the Vinaya Piṭaka and constitutes the ninth chapter of the *Cullavagga* [SuttaCentral; Hazra 1994; ICTS 2017]. The text regulates the procedures governing the suspension or cancellation of the fortnightly recitation of the Pātimokkha, permitting a monastic to exclude another who has unconfessed monastic offenses from participating [SuttaCentral]. In addition to these exclusion procedures, the chapter sets forth the essential personal qualities and ethical duties required of a monk before he attempts to reprove or correct another monastic [SuttaCentral]. It also incorporates an exposition on the eight wonderful qualities of the great ocean (*Mahāsamuddeatthacchariya*), which shares textual material with the *Pahārāda Sutta* (AN 8.19) and the *Uposatha Sutta* (AN 8.20 / Ud 5.5) [ICTS 2017; SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include the *Poṣadhasthāpanavastu* preserved in Sanskrit and Tibetan within the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya tradition, as well as corresponding Khandhaka sections in the Sarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Mahīśāsaka Vinayas in Chinese translation, and various sūtra parallels such as AN 8.20, EA 48.2, MA 37, T 33, T 34, and T 35 [SuttaCentral; Lueritthikul 2015]. Passage-level parallels exist with the *Udāna* (Ud 5.5), the *Kusinārasutta* (AN 10.44), the *Sirimaṇḍattheragāthā* (Thag 6.13), and the *Udānavarga* (UV 6) [SuttaCentral]. These correspondences are supported by DharmaNexus text-reuse computations, which show extensive Pali-internal sharing with AN 8 (AN 8.20), Ud 5.5, the *Upālipañcaka* (Pvr 17), and AN 10.44, along with cross-language alignments to the Sanskrit *Poṣadhasthāpanavastu*, the Tibetan *Vinayavastu*, and Chinese Āgama texts such as the *Zhanpo biqiu jing* (MA 37 / T 64) and *Zengyi ahan jing* (EA 48.2 / T 125) [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral]. The text has been studied comparatively against the Mūlasarvāstivāda *Poṣadhasthāpanavastu* by Phra Weerachai Lueritthikul, and has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [Lueritthikul 2015; SuttaCentral].
